scope: Local CPU benchmark migration and release validation; no full benchmark or Bayesian optimization run
checks: All 12 published benchmark Python sources compile
Both QM8 and QM9 CLI input checks pass on synthetic SMILES/label/XYZ fixtures with nine point features
Row/SMILES mismatches, reordered map rows, duplicate XYZ files, missing files, and path escapes are rejected
All seven nonempty modality combinations complete CPU forward and backward with finite outputs/gradients; multi-branch models select GatedFusion and absent branches receive zero gate weight
Seeded random splits are disjoint and sorted; full-pool retrieval and first-index tie handling pass
XYZ Fortran-style floats and centering pass; truncated and nonfinite coordinates are rejected
All six fusion choices across all seven nonempty modality combinations (42 cases) pass CPU forward/backward and strict state-dict reload with identical evaluation outputs
Six fusion choices preserve identically seeded encoder weights and the original five SMILES CNN kernels
Both feature gates export detached, normalized per-channel weights with zero weight for missing modalities; zero scalar logits exactly reproduce mean fusion
CLI fusion choices reach the run configuration and selected training script; non-default fusion output directories are isolated; invalid single-modality and CMCR combinations fail before data loading
limitations: The synthetic input check does not validate the historical full dataset, cleaned QM8 row mapping, or historical reported metrics.

The supplied Model_1.py and new Model.py default to concatenation; gate is an explicit publication default. The new gate initializes layers in a different order, so a fixed seed alone does not reproduce the previous initial weights or training trajectory.
Full end-to-end training, plotting/Excel export, CUDA execution, and optional Optuna trials were not run during packaging.
Historical Bayesian optimization provenance and upstream source licensing have not been established.
ast_comparison_scope: Compared with the supplied same-named source files. This compares top-level function/class definitions, not module-level training statements; CLI wiring and model-construction changes are also present. All eight encoder definitions remain unchanged from the original Model_1.py.

previous_gate_checkpoint_check.scope: Strict state-dict load and exactly equal eval predictions on all seven nonempty synthetic modality combinations; feature gate weights also exactly equal for every multi-branch case.
